content.title: Drugs and Other Substances With Potential to Impair BP Control
content.summary: This section discusses numerous substances, including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, herbals, and food substances, that may affect blood pressure (BP) control. It details the importance of a careful history in patients with hypertension to manage substances that might impair BP control, and emphasizes reducing or discontinuing such substances.

conditions.condition: Mineralocorticoid excess syndromes other than primary aldosteronism
conditions.clinical indications: Early-onset hypertension; resistant hypertension; hypokalemia or hyperkalemia
Acral features, enlarging shoe, glove, or hat size; headache, visual disturbances; diabetes mellitus
conditions.physical examination: Acral features; large hands and feet; frontal bossing
conditions.screening tests: Serum growth hormone ≥1 ng/mL during oral glucose load
conditions.additional tests: Elevated age- and sex-matched IGF-1 level; MRI scan of the pituitary
